title: Planning and Tool Use
description: Learn the ReAct pattern, how agents chain reasoning and action, and how memory supports multi-step workflows.

data.text: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning with action execution. The agent thinks aloud ("I need to find X"), invokes a tool ("search web for X"), observes the output, and updates its reasoning until the goal is met.

data.caption: ReAct loop: thought → action → observation → repeat

data.text: Common tools include: web search (find current facts), code execution (compute/verify), file system (read/write code), and API calls (integrate with third-party services). The agent must choose the right tool for each subtask and know when to stop.

Tool use introduces failure modes: wrong tool choice, malformed parameters, loops where the agent repeats the same action, and tool fatigue where context grows too large. Robust agents add tool-timeout limits, parameter validation, and max-step guards.

data.question: An agent needs to fix a test failure across three files and verify with a test runner. List three tools it needs and one memory detail it should retain between steps.
data.answer: Tools: file editor (read/write), test runner (execute tests), version control (git diff). Memory: the failing test name and expected assertion so it knows when the fix is complete.
